title: Postmortem: Embedding/rerank latency surge caused by shard compaction + fallback model mismatch
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2025-11-03 a sustained latency and error-rate increase affected the embeddings + reranking endpoint for approximately 3 hours. Root cause was an uncoordinated shard compaction job that triggered large in-memory index rebuilds on a subset of embedding nodes, causing memory pressure and evictions in the serving runtime. The autoscaler and circuit-breaker logic then evicted GPU-backed rerank workers, falling back to a CPU-quantized rerank model (rerank-lite-v2) which produced higher latency and lower-quality scores. Several customers observed timeouts and outlier score distributions leading to degraded user experiences.
impact: Between 2025-11-03T09:12 and 2025-11-03T12:25 UTC: 37% of rerank requests experienced >2x latency, head-of-line latency percentiles spiked (p50 from 120ms to 340ms, p95 from 420ms to 1600ms). Error rates (5xx) for the rerank route increased from 0.1% baseline to 2.8%. Three paying customers on Dedicated capacity reported production outages or degraded search relevance, triggering customer support escalations.
timeline: 2025-11-03 09:05 UTC: Scheduled compaction job (auto-maintenance) for embedding index shards started; job kicks off across 6 nodes in eu-west-1.
2025-11-03 09:12 UTC: Monitoring alert: gpu-memory-pressure on embeddings-node-23 and embeddings-node-24. Latency for /v1/rerank begins to climb.
2025-11-03 09:20 UTC: Autoscaler reacted to CPU and memory signals and drained two GPU workers; circuit breaker engaged on one remaining GPU pool due to OOM retries.
2025-11-03 09:27 UTC: Traffic routed to fallback path (cpu-quantized rerank-lite-v2). Relevance drift observed in customer dashboards; pager duty triggered.
2025-11-03 09:45 UTC: Incident declared. On-call and runtime teams begin mitigation. Temporary mitigation executed: cancel compaction jobs and rehydrate KV caches from snapshot.
2025-11-03 10:10 UTC: Rolling restart of affected embedding nodes to reclaim memory. Partial recovery in latency at 10:55 UTC but p95 remained elevated.
2025-11-03 11:30 UTC: Gradual failback to GPU rerank workers after health checks; traffic shifted back by 11:55 UTC.
2025-11-03 12:25 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline. Incident closed at 12:40 UTC after post-checks and customer triage.
2025-11-04 08:00 UTC: Post-incident review meeting: cross-team attendees from runtime, infra, embeddings, and product. Decided to produce this postmortem and action list.
root_cause: A maintenance compaction job for the embedding index started during a moderate traffic window without shard-level throttling. Compaction required transient memory allocations to build new index segments; on several older hosts (with lower headroom because of prior KV cache growth) this pushed GPU-hosted processes over memory thresholds. The serving runtime's protection logic interpreted repeated OOM/retry patterns as an unhealthy pool and drained GPU rerank workers. The fallback path used a CPU-quantized rerank variant that was not fully validated against the live embedding distribution, causing both latency and quality regressions.
mitigation_taken: 1) Immediately cancelled compaction and paused other background maintenance across embedding clusters. 2) Rehydrated KV cache from last good snapshot to avoid full rebuilds. 3) Forced a controlled rolling restart of the 6 affected embedding hosts to clear leaked allocations. 4) Manually disabled aggressive autoscaler triggers for rerank pools until thresholds were tuned. 5) Notified affected customers and provided interim mitigation guidance (increase timeouts, route to dedicated pools where possible).
long_term_fix: 1) Implement shard-level compaction throttling and maintenance window awareness tied to traffic/seasonal signals. 2) Add pre-checks for host memory headroom before starting large index operations and auto-stagger compaction across a wider time window. 3) Enhance runtime logic to distinguish index-compaction-induced memory spikes from actual service degradation to avoid unnecessary worker eviction. 4) Promote an explicitly validated CPU fallback model and run nightly A/B checks comparing rerank-lite variants to GPU reference on production-like embedding snapshots. 5) Improve observability: new dashboards that correlate compaction jobs, memory headroom, autoscaler decisions, and rerank quality metrics (score distribution, top-k stability).
action_items: AI-1: (Priority P0) Implement compaction pre-check gating: ensure host memory headroom >= 30% before compaction starts. Owner: Marisol Ortega. ETA: 2026-01-15.
AI-2: (Priority P1) Add stagger logic to maintenance orchestrator to never run compaction on >1/3 of shards in a placement unit simultaneously. Owner: Ravi Desai. ETA: 2026-02-01.
AI-3: (Priority P1) Runtime change: add a new health signal to prevent treating short-lived OOM during controlled rebuilds as permanent pool failure. Owner: Jonah Kim. ETA: 2025-12-18.

AI-4: (Priority P2) Create a nightly regression test that replays production embedding snapshots against CPU fallback models and records quality delta. Owner: Data Quality team (assigned: Lillian Ho). ETA: 2026-01-31.

AI-5: (Priority P2) Update customer incident runbook: recommend earlier routing to reserved Dedicated pools and include sample GraphQL query to toggle rerank timeout. Owner: Support Docs. ETA: 2025-11-24.
AI-6: (Priority P3) Perform capacity audit and upgrade a subset of older embedding hosts to reduce image/guest memory fragmentation. Owner: Infra ops. ETA: 2026-03-01.
postmortem_notes: During the review, engineering and product debated the trade-off between more aggressive compaction (smaller index, lower storage/cold-start cost) versus operational safety. We decided to relax compaction aggressiveness for high-traffic shards and prioritize predictability. The incident surfaced that the fallback path was treated as a drop-in replacement; future work will surface quantitative quality deltas during failovers so product teams can choose policies (latency-first vs quality-first).
follow_ups: We will run a canary for the new compaction gating logic on a single placement unit in eu-west-1 before rolling out globally. A post-action verification period of 90 days will track maintenance-triggered latency incidents. Support will proactively contact affected customers to review Dedicated routing and share the incident timeline.
notes_for_release: Include compaction-gating and autoscaler-signal changes in release notes for runtime-1.19. Ops should schedule a brief maintenance window announcement prior to rollout.
metrics_snapshot: Baseline p50:120ms p95:420ms error_rate:0.1% -> Incident peak p50:340ms p95:1600ms error_rate:2.8%. Index compaction started concurrent with 8GB resident memory increase on two hosts. GPU worker count dropped from 18 to 6 during event.
